accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Chola embassies to China:
1. Kulottunga I sent a 72-member merchant mission to China.
2. Rajaraja I sent embassies to China.
3. Rajendra I sent embassies to China.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Kulottunga I sent a 72-member merchant mission, while Rajaraja I and Rajendra I also sent embassies to China.
accepted.tq: Check each ruler separately before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: Which guild was primarily associated with foreign or long-distance trade?
accepted.x: Manigramam was a guild engaged in foreign or long-distance trade.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between long-distance trading guilds and local merchant assemblies.

accepted.s: The Ainnurruvar, known as the ‘Five Hundred’ of Ayyavole, was a
o: royal council concerned with temple architecture
powerful inter-regional and overseas merchant body
guild of Arab horse traders alone
accepted.x: The Ainnurruvar was a powerful inter-regional and overseas merchant body.
accepted.tq: Use the scale of activity—inter-regional and overseas—to identify the guild.

accepted.s: The name ‘Nanadesis’ most closely indicates merchants ‘of’
accepted.x: Nanadesis means merchants ‘of many countries’ and was associated with foreign trade.
accepted.tq: Use the literal qualification in the guild name to distinguish foreign traders from local assemblies.

accepted.s: What was the principal activity of the Nagaram?
o: Local merchant assembly and domestic trade in market towns
accepted.x: Nagaram was a local merchant assembly in market towns and was associated with domestic trade.
accepted.tq: Separate the local domestic role of Nagaram from the overseas role of other guilds.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Guild or body)
a. Manigramam
b. Ainnurruvar
c. Nanadesis
 d. Nagaram

List-II (Activity)
i. Local merchant assembly and domestic trade
 ii. Foreign or long-distance trade
 iii. Inter-regional and overseas trade
 iv. Foreign trade, meaning ‘of many countries’

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Manigramam handled foreign or long-distance trade; Ainnurruvar was inter-regional and overseas; Nanadesis represented merchants of many countries; Nagaram was local and domestic.
accepted.tq: Build the answer from the distinctive sure pair Nagaram–local domestic trade, then verify the remaining guilds.

accepted.s: As Chola power declined, the merchant guilds

accepted.tq: Identify the institutional change associated with the decline of central power.

accepted.x: The Nanadesi Pekkundru was the foreign-trade guild in Andhra, while the Nakaram was associated with domestic trade.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the comparative development of Dravidian art?
o: The Pallavas laid its foundation and the Cholas developed it on a monumental scale.
The Cholas laid its foundation and the Pallavas built its monumental culmination.
The Rashtrakutas alone created the Dravidian tradition.
The Hoysalas laid its foundation and the Kakatiyas completed it.
accepted.x: The comparison states that the Pallavas laid the foundation of Dravidian art, while the Cholas built its monumental culmination.
accepted.tq: Preserve the direction of the comparison instead of reversing the contributions of the Pallavas and Cholas.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
